summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared, writable, sticky-bit directory (mode 1777, root:root) so any user can create files but only the file owner (or root) can remove them. Verified the behavior before and after a full node restart, confirming both the sticky-bit protection and the restart/recovery persisted correctly.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop with mode 1777, owner root:root on node1
Created temporary test users dropuser1/dropuser2 to validate sticky-bit semantics
Confirmed dropuser2 could not delete dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted) but could create/delete its own files
Cleaned up test files and removed temporary test users
Captured pre-restart boot_id and /srv/drop state as baseline
Issued native reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (dfeb3b70... -> d19c6a2b...) proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions (1777 root:root) persisted after restart
Re-ran sticky-bit cross-user delete test post-restart with new temp users vuser1/vuser2, confirming same protected behavior, then cleaned up test artifacts and users

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit protecting cross-user deletion
evidence.summary: mkdir + chmod 1777 + chown root:root, confirmed via stat showing '1777 root root /srv/drop'
dropuser1 successfully created a file in /srv/drop

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users
evidence.summary: dropuser2 attempted rm on dropuser1's file; got 'Operation not permitted', exit code 1, file remained

evidence.requirement: Users can still remove their own files (directory remains normally usable)
evidence.summary: dropuser2 created and successfully deleted its own file, own_rm_exit=0

evidence.requirement: Healthy pre-restart baseline captured (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id dfeb3b70-bc1e-4ce9-90d0-9c9c853416e7 and confirmed /srv/drop perms 1777 root:root before restart
shutdown -r now issued via backgrounded nohup; connection dropped as expected, confirming the restart command was accepted and executing

evidence.requirement: Node polled until command execution available again
evidence.summary: First poll failed with connection reset (node still rebooting); second poll succeeded with 'up', confirming exec access restored

evidence.requirement: Proof that boot identity changed (real restart, not just service bounce)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id d19c6a2b-6c5d-43a9-9be9-492610903feb differs from pre-restart dfeb3b70-bc1e-4ce9-90d0-9c9c853416e7, and uptime -s shows a new boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config/data and re-verification of sticky-bit behavior
evidence.summary: /srv/drop retained 1777 root:root permissions after reboot; fresh cross-user test (vuser1/vuser2) reproduced correct sticky-bit protection (cross_rm_exit=1, own_rm_exit=0), then test artifacts and users were cleaned up leaving /srv/drop empty and correctly configured
